title: Random acts of kindness
paragraphs: It could happen anywhere at any time. It's often unexpected, but almost never unappreciated. Most people, at one time or another, have been on the receiving end of a random act of kindness - that moment of pure altruism when a complete stranger stops to offer aid, generosity or compassion. You may even be in a moment of dire need. In a sometimes callous world where people can be so focused on what they're doing, a random act of kindness can make all the difference.

They can be relatively insignificant. Hannah Bailey from London, for example, told the Metro newspaper about how she was given her fruit and vegetable shopping for free. The seller did her a kindness when it emerged she didn't have any change to pay. She was happy about it all day.

The city of Naples has long had a tradition called 'caffè sospeso'. When buying coffee, a person who has recently been lucky would purchase two cups but only drink one, leaving the second one anonymously, out of the goodness of their heart, for a poor person to claim for free. This tradition is now more common worldwide.

However, in some cases, these little acts can be a matter of life and death. Take, for example, the unnamed commuter, who in June 2018 fell off a station platform onto an electric railway track in Toronto, Canada. A quick-thinking, but even now unknown, bystander selflessly leapt down to pull him to safety.

Or Jonny Benjamin, who in London in 2008 was persuaded not to commit suicide by a passer-by. He had been considering jumping from a bridge. He later found the Good Samaritan and thanked him. He may one day find a way to pay him back in kind – though that's not the point.

So, why do it? Often, the acts aren't reciprocated. The people never meet again. According to UK charity The Mental Health Foundation, acts like these can "give our lives new purpose, show us other perspectives on our own problems and even make us feel euphoric."

So give it a try. Hold open a door for someone, deliver a compliment - even give up your seat on a bus. Help someone who is in need. It takes all kinds. It needn't be anything huge. One day, whether you need it or not, someone might help you in your hour of need.

vocabulary.translation: 像扶门这样的随意善举能照亮别人的一天。

vocabulary.entry: altruism [ˈæltruɪzəm] n. 利他主义；无私
vocabulary.example: True altruism involves helping others without expecting any reward.
vocabulary.translation: 真正的利他主义意味着帮助他人而不期待任何回报。

vocabulary.term: dire need [ˈdaɪə(r) niːd] 迫切需求
vocabulary.entry: dire need [ˈdaɪə(r) niːd] 迫切需求

vocabulary.translation: 难民们迫切需要干净的水和医疗用品。

vocabulary.translation: 他无视那个乞讨食物的流浪汉，真是冷漠无情。

vocabulary.entry: make all the difference [meɪk ɔːl ðə ˈdɪfrəns] 产生重大影响
vocabulary.example: Having a supportive teacher can make all the difference to a child's education.
vocabulary.translation: 有一位支持自己的老师，对孩子的教育能产生重大影响。

vocabulary.entry: insignificant [ˌɪnsɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt] adj. 微不足道的
vocabulary.example: The amount of money involved is insignificant compared to the overall budget.
vocabulary.translation: 与总预算相比，涉及的金额微不足道。

vocabulary.entry: caffè sospeso [kəˈfeɪ ˈsɒspesoʊ] 待领咖啡（意大利传统）
vocabulary.example: Caffè sospeso is a beautiful tradition where customers buy coffee for those who can't afford it.
vocabulary.translation: “待领咖啡”是一种美好的传统，顾客会为那些买不起咖啡的人买单。

vocabulary.term: anonymously [əˈnɒnɪməsli] adv. 匿名地
vocabulary.entry: anonymously [əˈnɒnɪməsli] adv. 匿名地
vocabulary.example: The whistleblower provided evidence anonymously to protect their identity.
vocabulary.translation: 举报人为保护自己的身份，匿名提供了证据。

vocabulary.entry: a matter of life and death [ə ˈmætə(r) ɒv laɪf ənd deθ] 生死攸关的事

vocabulary.translation: 对于被困在燃烧大楼里的人来说，逃生是生死攸关的事。

vocabulary.entry: quick-thinking [ˈkwɪk θɪŋkɪŋ] adj. 反应敏捷的

vocabulary.entry: selflessly [ˈselfləsli] adv. 无私地

vocabulary.translation: 一位好心人捡到了我丢失的钱包，并原封不动地还给了我。

vocabulary.term: pay back in kind [peɪ bæk ɪn kaɪnd] 以同样方式回报
vocabulary.entry: pay back in kind [peɪ bæk ɪn kaɪnd] 以同样方式回报

vocabulary.translation: 他们帮我们搬了家，我们为他们做了一顿饭作为回报。

vocabulary.entry: reciprocated [rɪˈsɪprəkeɪtɪd] adj. 被回报的；得到回应的（reciprocate 的过去分词）

vocabulary.translation: 当他在她困难时伸出援手时，她的善意终于得到了回报。

vocabulary.entry: perspectives [pəˈspektɪvz] n. 视角；观点（复数）

vocabulary.example: He delivered a genuine compliment about her hard work and dedication.
vocabulary.translation: 他真诚地赞美了她的努力和奉献精神。

vocabulary.term: in your hour of need [ɪn jɔː(r) ˈaʊə(r) ɒv niːd] 在你需要的时候
vocabulary.entry: in your hour of need [ɪn jɔː(r) ˈaʊə(r) ɒv niːd] 在你需要的时候
vocabulary.translation: 真正的朋友会在你需要的时候支持你。

vocabulary.example: The child leapt down from the low wall and ran towards his mother.
vocabulary.translation: 那个孩子从矮墙上跳下，朝他妈妈跑去。
